the ENU-induced molecular spectrum in Drosophila male germ cells is predominantly AT-->TA transversion, with a lower proportion of AT-->GC transitions.

the molecular mutation spectra in spermatogonia of D.melan-gaster and mouse are very similar and predominantly induced at AT sites, with AT-->GC transitions as the most frequent mutation, suggesting that the repair system is the major determinant of the mutagenic spectrum.
ENU-induced mutation spectra in pre-meiotic Drosophila spermatogonias show a predominance of AT-->TA transversion and AT-->GC transition mutations.

the study of the mechanisms involved in the induction of mutations by chemical carcinogens.
the study of the molecular mechanisms involved in the mutagenicity and carcinogenicity of chemical carcinogens.

the spectrum of ENU-induced mutations is dependent on the stage and the system analyzed, but that the major mutagenic events are A:T-->T:A transversions and A:T-->G:C transitions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spectrum of mutations induced by alkylating agents in Drosophila and in mouse is very similar, and that the differences between them are mainly due to the efficiency of DNA repair in these two species.
ENU is a very efficient mutagen in pre-meiotic Drosophila germ cells.

in vivo ENU induces a spectrum of mutations that is similar in Drosophila pre-meiotic germ cell stages and in mouse spermatogonias, with the most mutagenicity in AT pairs, and that these results are consistent with the adduct spectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mutation spectrum of ENU is similar in both Drosophila and mouse.
ENU-induced mutations are not only dependent on the type of adducts formed but also on the type of cells in which the mutagenic events occur.
